verdicts.reading: In 1988 the feared generalised (explosive) heterosexual AIDS epidemic in America and Europe starts to look less likely, i.e. heterosexual spread stays confined and does not take off in the general population.
verdicts.reason: 'Threat of a heterosexual epidemic' in 1987 usage meant the feared generalised spread to the general population; that reading dominates over a reading on the heterosexual share of cases, which the text does not name. CDC 1988 update: heterosexually acquired cases 4.8% of adult cases in 1988 vs 5.2% in 1983, concentrated in discrete groups (partners of IV-drug users, Black/Hispanic women). No generalised epidemic took off in the US or western Europe. A's divergence rests on a rising heterosexual share in the 1990s, which is a different measure (and beyond the D27 window), so no second equally faithful reading. Low-medium certainty: 'threat' is partly perceptual.
